question.leadin: A number of emperors named Jayavarman once ruled the territory that is this modern day nation.
question.text: Name this Southeast Asian Nation where one could find the massive temple complex of Angkor Wat or visit its capital, Phnom Penh.
question.clue: One leader of this country tried to cleanse the country and start over with a "Year Zero."

swap.leadin: The American evacuation from this country was signaled by the playing of Irving Berlin's "White Christmas" on the radio in April.
swap.text: Name this country where helicopters extracted over 2,000 people in Operation Frequent Wind in 1975, marking the end of American involvement in a Southeast Asian war.
swap.clue: The Le Dynasty was nominally in control of this country for over 300 years.

question.text: The victims of the Kent State shooting were protesting the bombing of Cambodia during this war. Boxer Muhammad Ali was jailed for refusing to be drafted to fight in this war.
question.clue: Students at an Iowa high school wore black armbands in protest of this war, and William Calley was convicted for a massacre in the Son Tinh district in this war.

swap.text: Massacres of PKI members occurred after the failure of the 30th September movement, which aimed to overthrow this first President of Indonesia, who formulated the Pancasila.
swap.clue: His state philosophy was known as Pancasila, or Five Principles, and he was forced to declare his nationa's independence by a 1945 kidnapping.

question.text: After the war, American forces faced a rebellion in the newly conquered Philippines that ended with the surrender of this first Filipino president.
question.clue: Earlier, he quarreled with Andres Bonifacio over divisions in the Katipunan movement.

swap.leadin: This is the largest religious complex in the world.
swap.text: Name this structure built to resemble Mount Meru, a temple to Vishnu made by Suryavarman II. This structure was later converted to a Buddhist temple after the capital city it was part of fell to the Cham.
swap.clue: This structure, which is designed to resemble the axis mundi, contains reliefs depicting the churning of the sea of milk.

question.text: Indonesia was ruled from 1967 until 1999 by this controversial president, whose support eroded after the Asian Financial Crisis. He established the New Order and took power in the wake of the 30 September coup attempt.
question.clue: He was propelled to power by the 30 September Movement, marking the end of "Guided Democracy" and the beginning of the "New Order" period.

swap.leadin: A rickshaw-like vehicle known as the becak was ubiquitous in this city before they were banned in the 1970s.
swap.text: Name this city whose skyline is dominated by the mortar-and-pestle-shaped Monas monument, which was built during the rule of Sukarno. It is the capital of Indonesia.
swap.clue: Government buildings are housed near its enormous Merdeka Square, which is home to the flame-topped Monas obelisk.

question.leadin: This woman was put under house arrest after calling for democracy in front of the Shwedagon Pagoda in the aftermath of the 8888 Uprising.
question.text: Name this founder of the National League for Democracy whose efforts to democratize her home country were opposed by the State Peace and Development Council, a military junta.
question.answerHtml: Aung San Suu Kyi [do not prompt on "Aung" or "San" or "Aung San"]
question.clue: This leader allegedly called two Reuters journalists "traitors" after they were arrested while investigating the Inn Din Massacre.

swap.leadin: Approximately one hundred thousand people have been displaced in the Kachin war, which re-ignited in June 2011 as one of many theaters of this country's civil war.
swap.text: Name this country in which Aung San Suu Kyi leads the National League for Democracy.
swap.answerHtml: Union of Burma [or Pyidaungzu Myanma Naingngandaw; or Union of Myanmar]
swap.clue: This country's "Way to Socialism" was advocated for by its dictator Ne Win.

question.leadin: This country's namesake Solidarity Convention formed in 1965 to oppose ethnic discrimination.
question.text: Name this country, whose Constitution's Article 153 gives its native Bumiputera ("boo-mee-POO-teh-ruh") people preferred status. Race riots in 1969 forced the resignation of this country's first Prime Minister, Tunku Abdul Rahman.
question.clue: The location of the Langkasuka kingdom, its eponymous language is first attested on the Kedukan Bukit inscription.

swap.leadin: In many local legends, two figures with this surname turned into statues after they died from jumping into the Hat Giang River.
swap.text: Give this surname of two sisters who led a 43 CE rebellion against forces led by Ma Yuan. Today, they are national heroes of Vietnam.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the adventures of Chinese pirate lords.
question.text: This dynasty's Pham Quang Anh ["fam gwang on"] scouted the Paracel and Spratly Islands for pirate hideouts. The last king of this dynasty founded by Gia Long ["zah long"] was the King of Tonkin under French protection and was named Bao Dai.
question.clue: An ambassador reluctantly serving this dynasty wrote an epic about a woman forced into prostitution by her husband, Scholar Ma, in the Tale of Kieu.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Hindu kingdoms outside the Indian subcontinent.
swap.text: This kingdom in modern-day Vietnam was surrounded by the Khmer empire and Đai Viet until it was annexed in 1471 by Vietnamese emperor Le Nhan Tong. This kingdom's king Bhadravarman I built the My Son ("mee sun") temple complex.
swap.clue: Upon conquering the neighbouring Funan Kingdom, Shaivism became the state religion, and the kingdom was involved in the Spice Route as a producer of aloe.

question.leadin: An empire centered in this modern-day country was ruled by kings named Jayavarman.
question.text: Name this modern-day country that contained the center of the Khmer empire. Suryavarman II built this country's Angkor Wat.
question.clue: This nation fought a long-running war with its neighbor, Vietnam, from 1979 to 1991, which had invaded in order to end the violent government of Pol Pot, the Khmer Rouge {KUH-MEER - ROOZ}.

swap.leadin: A king of this dynasty founded an order of Buddhism called Dhammayut and served as the first abbot of the Wat Bowonniwet Vihara ("WAHT buh-NAH-wet wah-HEE-ruh").
swap.text: Name this dynasty whose viceroy Pinklao was the younger brother of King Mongkut, who negotiated the Bowring Treaty liberalizing foreign trade.
swap.clue: This dynasty's first ruler solidified power by winning the Nine Armies War, and it allowed free trade within its territory by agreeing to the Bowring Treaty, which replaced the Burney Treaty.

question.leadin: In an iconic sculpture, this king is depicted pouring a goblet of water on the ground, showing that he no longer considered himself subject to the Burmese lords of the Toungoo Dynasty.
question.text: Name this great ruler of the Ayutthaya Kingdom, known as the "Black Prince," who was taken hostage as a child by the Burmese king Bayinnaung, only to return and reclaim his homeland.

swap.text: This Thai dictator was in power when the helpfully-named Coup Group solidified military control of the country in the Silent Coup. He changed the country's name from "Siam" via a series of "cultural mandates" and fought the 1940 Franco-Thai War.

question.text: Along with the islands in the Labuan territory, East Malaysia is made up of these two states found on the north of the island of Borneo.
question.answerHtml: Sabah and Sarawak [order not important but don't accept or prompt on just one]

swap.text: Later, the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824 settled whether this region fell under the sphere of influence of the Dutch or British companies. Stamford Raffles negotiated its sultan, Hussain Shah for the land of Singapore.
